decision.reason: The MessageDB adapter is deprecated and will not ship in the release candidate.

findings.claim: An obsolete linked master mailbox can become unreachable during garbage collection and kill the caller while processors remain healthy.
findings.invariant: Dropping all references except the bare waitApp action must not allow garbage collection to kill its caller.

findings.claim: The review covered the named master module, not package-wide security, throughput, allocation, every shutdown interleaving, or every adapter.
findings.invariant: The final verdict names unexecuted scope and never promotes a module review to package-wide certification.

disposition.rationale: The broader initiative supplies the missing matrix and preserves the original review boundary.

findings.claim: A reachability-sensitive regression is valid only when the observer and cleanup path do not retain the application handle.
findings.invariant: Every GC-liveness matrix cell runs in a separate process and retains only the action under test.

disposition.rationale: ADR 0001 makes this a durable test-design constraint.

findings.claim: An adapter shutdown exception or cancellation during drain bypasses later adapter shutdown and supervisor cleanup.
findings.invariant: All acquired adapters are signalled and the supervisor is stopped even when shutdown throws or is cancelled, while the original exception is preserved.

findings.claim: Duplicate processor IDs start multiple processors and silently discard earlier lifecycle handles.
findings.invariant: Duplicate ordinary, batch, and mixed processor IDs are rejected before any startup effect.

findings.claim: Cancellation between master acquisition, child creation, and handle transfer may leak supervised resources.
findings.invariant: Startup cancellation at every ownership-transfer boundary leaves no master or child thread running.

findings.claim: The existing timeout bounds drain after adapter shutdown returns; it is not a total shutdown deadline.
findings.invariant: The release documents and tests the chosen total shutdown bound separately from the drain timeout.

findings.claim: Runtime reproduction confirms a throwing adapter prevents later shutdown calls and application completion.
findings.invariant: All adapter shutdown actions and supervisor cleanup run despite one shutdown exception.

findings.claim: Runtime reproduction confirms duplicate IDs let waitApp complete while an earlier processor remains unrepresented and unsignalled.
findings.invariant: Identity validation precedes all processor and adapter startup effects.

findings.claim: Startup acquisition and ownership transfer are not masked, so asynchronous cancellation can bypass cleanup.
findings.invariant: Cancellation during startup cleans every acquired resource exactly once.

findings.claim: Concurrent and batch halt writes do not wake blocked intake, so an idle source can prevent completion indefinitely.
findings.invariant: Acknowledged halt wakes Serial, Ahead, Async, partitioned, and batch processors without requiring later source activity.

findings.claim: Exhausted finalizer retries are converted to requested halt and reported as graceful completion.
findings.invariant: Infrastructure finalization failure remains a failure under every supervision strategy and is never reported as AckHalt.

findings.claim: A keyed worker exception is retained until input exhaustion, so unending input can defer it indefinitely while more work runs.
findings.invariant: The first keyed worker failure stops intake, settles owned children, and propagates without waiting for upstream exhaustion.

findings.claim: An unmasked interval between async allocation and worker-map insertion may leave an untracked start-gate waiter after cancellation.
findings.invariant: Worker allocation and registration transfer ownership atomically under cancellation.

findings.claim: Nonpositive Ahead and Async values are accepted and can select default or unlimited concurrency.
findings.invariant: Nonpositive concurrency and overflowing derived capacities are rejected before startup in every processing mode.

findings.claim: Successful later bursts inherit an old activity timestamp and healthy sustained work can be reported stuck.
findings.invariant: Readiness distinguishes absence of progress from both fresh bursts and sustained healthy throughput.

findings.claim: A concurrent metrics sample is not guaranteed to be a cross-field transactional snapshot.
findings.invariant: Tests assert stable lifecycle meaning rather than exact equality among concurrently sampled fields.

disposition.rationale: This is an intentional sampling contract, not evidence of durable acknowledgement.

findings.claim: Batch processed and failed counters describe decisions, not confirmed durable finalization.
findings.invariant: Metrics documentation and release evidence do not equate handler decisions with durable acknowledgement.

disposition.rationale: The distinction is a documented semantic boundary.

findings.claim: Failed processors unregister from the metrics map, allowing readiness to report success with zero known processors.
findings.invariant: Readiness retains configured identities and terminal outcomes and distinguishes intentionally empty from unexpectedly missing workers.

findings.claim: Liveness reports success after master shutdown because it proves only that a metrics TVar can be read.
findings.invariant: Health reports the defined process and worker lifecycle states rather than successful access to stale shared memory.

findings.claim: Dependency health checks run sequentially and rely on providers for deadlines and exception normalization.
findings.invariant: The published health contract states and tests its dependency deadline and exception behavior.

findings.claim: The metrics package has no Cabal test suite, so none of its routes, encoders, or WebSocket behavior run in the release gate.
findings.invariant: The release gate executes a metrics suite that characterizes every published HTTP route, encoder, and WebSocket frame.

findings.claim: Handshake, snapshot, push, cancellation, and goodbye failures can skip connection-slot release.
findings.invariant: Every WebSocket exit returns the acquired connection slot to zero and structurally terminates its push child.

findings.claim: The WebSocket enable flag does not prevent upgrade handling.
findings.invariant: Disabled WebSocket configuration rejects all upgrade requests without acquiring a slot.

findings.claim: Unsubscribe-all leaves subscriptions as Nothing, which the push loop interprets as all processors.
findings.invariant: Unsubscribe-all suppresses processor updates until a later explicit subscription.

findings.claim: Delta-only clients receive no removal notification and can retain stale processor entries.
findings.invariant: The release verdict names this protocol limitation unless a removal or snapshot protocol is deliberately added.

findings.claim: A buffered later retry can overwrite the earliest unresolved offset and permit commit past unresolved work.
findings.invariant: The earliest unresolved offset remains a barrier until that delivery succeeds, regardless of later buffered finalization.

findings.claim: Exhausted acknowledgement failure can be stored for a source step that never occurs after source termination.
findings.invariant: Finalization failure is observed through drain completion even when the source has already terminated.

findings.claim: The adapter supports serial processing only, has no actual DLQ producer, and provides no cooperative-rebalance fencing.
findings.invariant: Tests and release claims remain inside these documented adapter contracts.

disposition.rationale: Serial processing and the absence of a DLQ producer remain explicit boundaries. The prior lack of cooperative-rebalance fencing is remediated when callers install kafkaRebalanceHandler; live two-consumer evidence proves the old owner's callback is rejected.

findings.claim: Shutdown commits before core draining and later stored offsets rely on auto-commit or consumer closure.
findings.invariant: Live-broker shutdown evidence demonstrates no unresolved offset is skipped under the documented commit timing.

disposition.rationale: Live buffered-retry, restart, idle-shutdown, and repeated-shutdown cases preserve the documented close-time commit contract without skipping unresolved work.

findings.claim: An ambiguous successful PostgreSQL commit followed by a retryable client error can duplicate a DLQ copy.
findings.invariant: DLQ movement is durably idempotent across lost commit confirmation and retry.

findings.claim: Prefetched deliveries may remain invisible until visibility timeout after shutdown; this is delayed redelivery, not deletion.
findings.invariant: Restart tests observe eventual redelivery within the declared visibility bound.

findings.claim: A single AckHandle is not internally serialized, while core is assumed to finalize each delivery sequentially.
findings.invariant: The adapter either enforces or explicitly tests and documents the sequential finalization precondition.

disposition.rationale: No core-triggered concurrent finalization was established.

findings.claim: Automatic dead-letter failure is reported only through a callback whose default does nothing, while the source message remains replayable.
findings.invariant: Failure visibility and eventual source-message recovery are both exercised under the configured callback policy.

findings.claim: Sparse category global positions permanently pin checkpoints.
findings.invariant: The excluded adapter must not be listed as certified or included in the candidate manifest.

findings.claim: A pending retry can make shutdown spin forever.
findings.invariant: The excluded adapter must not be listed as certified or included in the candidate manifest.

findings.claim: An idle source ignores shutdown until a message is produced.
findings.invariant: The excluded adapter must not be listed as certified or included in the candidate manifest.

findings.claim: Checkpoint state advances destructively before persistence succeeds and persister failure is unobserved.
findings.invariant: The excluded adapter must not be listed as certified or included in the candidate manifest.

findings.claim: DLQ writes are best effort, retry capacity excludes the unbounded TChan, and category grouping does not distribute a single category.
findings.invariant: The excluded adapter and its documented resource and durability limitations remain visible in the final verdict.

findings.claim: Consumer-group acquisition and cleanup are not exception safe, so cancellation or cleanup failure can strand subscriptions.
findings.invariant: Failure or cancellation at every member acquisition boundary terminates every acquired subscription while preserving the original error.

findings.claim: AckHalt cancels without checkpoint advancement and immediate shutdown can replay late work.
findings.invariant: Integration tests preserve the explicit replay and missing-checkpoint policy in mori://shinzui/kiroku/okf/adrs/concepts/ADR-4.

disposition.rationale: At-least-once replay is an intentional checkpoint contract.

findings.claim: No live database integration or exact checkpoint durability certification was performed.
findings.invariant: The real-store restart matrix proves acknowledgement and checkpoint recovery before certification.

findings.claim: Adapter documentation still claims supervised handler exceptions are not finalized, although current core converts them to AckRetry.
findings.invariant: Published adapter documentation matches the candidate core's handler-exception behavior.

findings.claim: The master-loop removal passes the isolated no-retained-handle GC regression and the ordinary core suite.
findings.invariant: The candidate continues to pass the original isolated GC regression.

disposition.rationale: This is positive historical evidence with an explicitly narrow scope.

findings.claim: Approval of the removed actor does not approve App ownership, halt, finalization, health, or all supervisor states.
findings.invariant: Integrated certification depends on every active child and every mandatory matrix cell, not REV-14 alone.

disposition.rationale: The MasterPlan explicitly preserves the narrow approval boundary.

findings.claim: User handlers in uninterruptible operations cannot be guaranteed to stop within a library timeout.
findings.invariant: Shutdown guarantees state their behavior when user code is uninterruptible and tests do not claim an impossible hard bound.

disposition.rationale: This is a runtime boundary that must be documented rather than hidden.

findings.claim: The completed-batch queue can exceed configured capacity by one emission burst.
findings.invariant: Memory budgets account for the documented burst rather than treating the capacity as a strict element bound.

disposition.rationale: The bounded overshoot is documented design behavior.

findings.claim: Distinct in-progress batch keys are not bounded by inbox capacity and can retain substantial memory.
findings.invariant: Candidate soak evidence measures high-cardinality batching and reports the supported memory envelope.

findings.claim: Ticker exceptions are not independently monitored by the output loop; no failing supported configuration was demonstrated.
findings.invariant: The candidate either reproduces and fixes a reachable ticker failure or records evidence that supported configurations cannot trigger it.

findings.claim: A childless NQE supervisor linked to the caller can become unreachable and kill that caller during garbage collection.
findings.invariant: Finished, halted, and failed applications may drop their handles without later killing the runApp caller during forced major collections.

findings.claim: The supervisor link and processor link deliver one StopAllOnFailure exception twice.
findings.invariant: One processor failure reaches the caller exactly once while siblings still stop.

findings.claim: The live-child GC regression and childless GC regression exercise different reachability states and both remain mandatory.
findings.invariant: The integrated matrix runs both isolated GC suites and the single-delivery lifecycle case.

disposition.rationale: The two tests prove distinct ownership states.

boundaries.description: Configuration validation, master acquisition, processor registration, and ownership transfer.
Source polling, bounded admission, shutdown wakeups, and leased-message replay.
Handler dispatch, bounded concurrency, result collection, and stop propagation.
Per-key serialization, pending work, worker registration, and worker failure.
Batch accumulation, tick/flush behavior, bounded output, and high-cardinality memory.
Retry scheduling, lease retention, exhausted retries, and shutdown of delayed work.
Ack, retry, halt, and dead-letter finalizers including exhausted infrastructure failures.
Graceful drain, adapter shutdown, force-stop, cancellation, and total deadline.
IgnoreFailures and StopAllOnFailure propagation, sibling cleanup, and GC-sensitive ownership.
Activity accounting, configured identities, terminal outcomes, readiness, and liveness.
Upgrade gating, connection slots, snapshot/push children, subscriptions, and disconnect cleanup.
Offset barriers, seek/replay, finalizer failure, rebalance, and committed acknowledgement state.
Visibility leases, transactional DLQ movement, ambiguous commits, outage recovery, and restart.
Subscription acquisition, acknowledgement coupling, checkpoint policy, cleanup, and restart.
Deprecated MessageDB checkpoint, retry, shutdown, and DLQ behavior.
